chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
One does not marry by Mut'a with the slave girl except with the permission of her owner.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for marrying a slave girl through Mut'a?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the juristic requirement that the owner's consent is a prerequisite for the validity of Mut'a with a slave girl, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where ownership alone suffices. This ruling underscores the economic and social dynamics of the time, ensuring that the master's property rights are respected while granting the slave girl the specific legal protection of her owner's approval for temporary union.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not marry by Mut’a with the slave girl except with the permission of her owner’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Marriage in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) is not permissible with a slave-girl without the permission of her people.’”
